questions.q: An Escalations team needs visibility into every Case marked Priority = Critical, regardless of who owns the case. Which type of sharing rule fits this requirement?
options: Owner-based sharing rule
Criteria-based sharing rule
Manual sharing
Controlled by Parent
questions.explain: Because the requirement depends on a field value (Priority = Critical) rather than who owns the record, a criteria-based sharing rule is the right tool — it shares records matching specific field values independent of ownership.

questions.q: What is the maximum access level a standard sharing rule can grant?
options: Read Only or Read/Write — nothing finer-grained is available
Full object-level administrative access
Read/Write/Transfer, matching the Leads and Cases OWD option
Whatever access level matches the target group's highest profile permission
questions.explain: A sharing rule's access-level ceiling is Read Only or Read/Write — there's no option for a more granular or more powerful access level through the standard sharing-rule configuration.

questions.q: A requirement calls for sharing one specific record with one specific named individual, as a one-off grant. Why is a sharing rule the wrong tool for this?
options: Sharing rules can only be created by a system administrator profile
Sharing rules cannot be applied to custom objects
Sharing rules only ever target a role, public group, or territory — never an individual named user directly
Sharing rules always apply to every record in the object, with no way to target a single record
questions.explain: Sharing rules are designed around reusable populations on both sides — a role, group, or territory — not individual named users. A one-off grant to a specific person is what manual sharing exists for instead.

questions.q: Which of these would trigger Salesforce to recalculate sharing for records governed by an owner-based sharing rule?
options: A user logs in from a new IP address
A page layout is updated for the object
A new field is added to an unrelated object
A user's role or group membership changes
questions.explain: Recalculation is triggered by changes that could affect the rule's outcome — the rule's own definition changing, group/role membership changing, or (for owner-based rules) a record's owner changing. Unrelated configuration changes like a page layout edit don't trigger it.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what's the honest test for whether a requirement actually needs Apex managed sharing instead of a declarative sharing rule?
options: Whether the admin personally prefers writing code
Whether the requirement depends on logic a declarative criteria filter genuinely cannot express, such as multi-object lookups or external data
Whether the object involved is a standard object rather than a custom object
Whether the sharing needs to be visible in Setup at all
questions.explain: Declarative sharing rules should always be considered first since they're visible in Setup, admin-maintainable, and automatically recalculated. Apex managed sharing is justified only when the logic genuinely can't be expressed as a declarative owner- or criteria-based rule.
